# Worlds: making each biome a place (2026-11-19)

Goal (owner): the environments should transport the player to another world. A world is not a recolour. Each one needs its own sky and horizon, light, ground and road, trees and props, weather and particles, a transition into it, and its own sound. Source of truth: Godot's `Themes.gd`, `ThemeFX.gd`, `DhJourney.gd`, `RunRig.gd`. Courses are dumped from the real generator (`godot/tests/dump_long.gd`, env `THEME=<id> WINDING=1`).

## Courses (all generated by Godot, seed 11, winding trail, 18 rows = 3.2 km)

`?course=long_alpine | long_candy | long_egypt | long_tunnel | long_desert | long_matrix | long_synthwave | long_w11` (long_w11 = psychedelic). The default `long_s7` is the old wide, nearly straight psychedelic course.

## Status per world

| World | Ground (Godot pattern, kept quiet) | Road | Sky | Trees | Seen by eye |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alpine | natural terrain: snow, grass, earth by slope | dark grey, white lines | Godot procedural sky: blue top, peach horizon, low sun | dumped materials | yes |
| Candy | swirled frosting bands, sprinkles | berry-brown, cream lines | pastel sky, pale sun | each tree its own sweet (by position) | yes (ground, sky, road) |
| Egypt | dune bands, dashes, grain | packed sandstone, pale gold lines | blue to gold horizon, pale sun | turquoise and gold | compile only |
| Tunnel | dark floor, neon chevrons | black, neon cyan lines (glow) | rays converging on the vanishing point | striped glowing columns | compile only |
| Desert | poster bands (sand, rust, teal) with contours | asphalt grey, white lines | huge red sun in rippling stripes | cactus green with ribs | compile only |
| Matrix | code falling down each column | black, green lines (glow) | code falling down the sky | scan-lit green | compile only |
| Synthwave | neon lattice, checker squares | dark, magenta lines (glow) | striped sun that never sets | hot pink to cyan | compile only |
| Psychedelic | natural terrain by region (frozen look kept elsewhere) | dark grey, white lines | its own | its own | yes |

The trip picture pass (warp, colour split, tracers) now runs only in the worlds Godot gives it: psychedelic and tunnel (`Themes.post_mode`). Matrix (mode 2) and synthwave (mode 3) have their own passes in Godot that are not ported yet; until then those two have none.

## What is still missing before a world feels like a place

1. **Horizon landmarks.** Godot builds them: pyramids (`Themes.pyramid_mesh`), candy hills (`candy_hills_mesh`), fluffy cotton trees and gumdrop rocks (`fluffy_tree_mesh`, `gumdrop_mesh`). Check which are in the dumps and render them; the mountain ring is still the plain white one in the non-psychedelic worlds.
2. **Weather and particles.** Egypt: the sandstorm that rolls in every 55 s for 14 s (`ThemeFX`, the gates and signs stay readable). Matrix: falling code in the air. Candy: drifting sprinkles. Desert: heat shimmer. Alpine: light snow.
3. **The other post passes** (matrix mode 2, synthwave mode 3) from `ThemePost.gd`.
4. **Transitions.** Godot's journey stages a world swap: sky first (0 to 0.30 of the onset), then ground (0.30 to 0.55), then trees (0.55 to 0.80), then light (0.80 to 1.0). `worldfx2` has `setStage(part, on)`. This is how you leave one world and arrive in another: build it on the journey director, not a hard cut.
5. **Sound.** A music and ambience bed per world (wind in alpine, desert wind, digital hum, synth pad). Not started.
6. **Gates, signs, hazards in each world's style** (`hazard_skin`: mummies in Egypt, etc.).
7. **Colour grade per world** from each theme's env (`saturation`, `contrast`, `glow`, `fog`, sun): the dumps carry them; check they are all applied.
8. **Each world's roads and regions.** The regions (pines, fever, dusk, blossom, under, ember) only drive the natural-terrain style; the other worlds ignore them.

## Order of work

Seen-by-eye pass on the five worlds not yet viewed, then landmarks, weather, post passes, then transitions and sound.


## Update: landmarks and weather (built, 2026-11-19)

| World | Landmark on the horizon | Weather in the air |
|---|---|---|
| Alpine | the original snow mountains; Godot's procedural sky | light falling snow (Godot's own: 600 quads, 76 x 30 x 76 m box) |
| Candy | candy hills (Godot's `candy_hills_mesh`), pastel, with haze | sprinkles in the candy colours |
| Egypt | pyramids (Godot's `pyramid_mesh`), sandstone with block courses and a gold tip | the sandstorm: every 55 s, 14 s long, fog goes thick and gold, wind-blown sand, `SANDSTORM! follow the beams` |
| Desert | mesas in strata of sand, rust and teal with contour lines | warm dust blowing across, motes rising |
| Tunnel | dark walls banded in neon | light streaks rushing toward you |
| Matrix | black data towers with scan lines and falling code | green code falling in streaks |
| Synthwave | neon wireframe mountains with a hot haze | neon motes drifting up |

Where it lives: `rings.js` (the horizon materials), `weather.js` (particles and the sandstorm), `biomes.js` (skies and trees), `gv.js` (ground styles). Godot's own landmarks for Egypt and candy are now in the courses as the camera-following horizon (the splitter recognises the mesh at y = -160). The terrain skirt (the sloping sides) wears each world's ground. `?noweather` and `?plainring` switch these off.

Bugs fixed on the way: the horizon material was being applied to every mesh (it blacked out candy's ground), the psychedelic sky's nebula showed in every world, and the splitter dropped the Egypt and candy horizons into row 0.

Seen by eye after the fixes: candy, egypt, tunnel, matrix. Not re-checked since: alpine, desert, synthwave.

Still missing: world transitions, per-world sound, the matrix and synthwave picture passes, and a coloured haze at the top of the sky in matrix and tunnel that I haven't traced.


## Update: barrier course and caverns (2026-11-19, late)

`?course=bar_psy`: Godot's barrier-and-gates course (psychedelic, 39 rows, 7 km), dumped with `BARRIER=1`. Built: the splitter recognises the realms' ground (`ALBEDO = c * 0.4`); `realms.js` ports the realm ground (vertex-coloured, emissive) and the glow shader (rim light, beat pulse, vertex wobble from vertex alpha); the roofed realms (glowcave, crystal, lava, abyss) dim the picture while you are inside (exposure and fog colour from `Realms.ROOF`) and show Godot's reveal line (`THE GROTTO WAKES`, ...).

Checked by eye: the Glow Grotto row (dark chamber, three gates in a row = a fork, exposure 0.42). Not checked: steering through the gates, the other realms (crystal, abyss, hive, canyon, mammoth, interzone, eyes, highway, mandala, melt) by eye, the props inside the grotto (the mushrooms and vines), collisions with the walled corridors.

Next: per-theme barrier courses, the live world swap on one course, the journey director.


## Update: walking the realms (2026-11-19, 22:00 to 23:00 session)

Found and fixed:
- **All multimeshes in barrier dumps had every instance at the origin** (the headless dump cannot read them back), so the barrier tree lines, rocks, forest sides and every realm prop were missing. Fix: `DownhillRig._add_mm` keeps a copy of the transforms and colours when `DownhillRig.keep_dump_data` is set (tests only), and `dump_long.gd` reads that copy. 9,753 instances now sit at their real positions across 7 km.
- Realm rows now carry their props: giant glowing mushrooms in the Glow Grotto, jellyfish, coral and stalactites in the Jelly Abyss, crystal clusters in the Crystal Vault, posts in the canyon, pillars in the interzone.
- One barrier course per world: `bar_psy`, `bar_alpine`, `bar_candy`, `bar_egypt`, `bar_tunnel`, `bar_desert`, `bar_matrix`, `bar_synthwave` (39 rows, 7 km each), all in the launcher.

Walked by eye on `bar_psy`: rush, highway, air, glowcave, abyss, drop, forest, crystal, hive, canyon, interzone, mammoth, tunnel, eyes. An unattended board rides through six zones in 40 s with 6 hits (it cannot choose gates, so a player does much better).

Not checked: the other seven barrier worlds by eye, lava, mandala, melt (not in this seed), and the 'eyes' realm's giant eyes (the eye props come from `row.eyes`, built separately).

Also done in that session: `bar_psy77` (seed 77) carries the Lava Tube, The Melt and the Orchard of Eyes (7 eyes on stalks in a row); all eight world barrier courses compile with no shader errors and were seen by eye (psy, candy, egypt, synthwave, tunnel, desert, matrix, alpine). The trail courses (`long_*`, default `long_s7`) were re-checked after the loader changes: no errors. Mandala Drop did not occur in any of seeds 11, 23, 42 or 77 (it is rare); to see it, dump more seeds with `BARRIER=1 SEED=n`.

Steering in barrier courses (late addition): the gates are lock-on targets (lean toward one and the board carves through it, Godot's "eyes choose, the board carves"), and barrier courses default to direct steering instead of the `aim` mode, which pulled the board back to the trail centre between gates. A crude simulated player (digital lean toward the good gate) takes 5 hits in 42 s against 6 for an unattended board; a person should do much better. `?assist=aim|lane|free` overrides.

Mandala Drop: Godot's own default zone weight for it is 0.0 (`DEFAULT_ZONE_WEIGHTS`, RunRig.gd), so the generator never picks it unless forced (`?realm=mandala`). It is switched off in Godot, not missing in our port. Left out on purpose.

Bug fixed (22:30): `?row=N` spawned the board at y=0 because the ground under the start row had not loaded, so it fell ~1,300 m through the realm. The start now waits for the ground, and the row loader follows the start position until the board is placed. Lava Tube seen by eye after the fix: red glowing floor, dark red roof, exposure 0.55.

Walk of the other barrier worlds (22:45), each started with `?row=` and ridden a few seconds, on the ground, no shader errors: egypt (Glow Grotto), matrix (canyon, code sky, pale posts), synthwave (Crystal Vault), desert (interzone, swirled red sky), tunnel (mammoth garden, neon rings), alpine (Jelly Abyss under snowfall). Realms look the same in every world, as in Godot (they have their own shaders); only the sky, horizon, weather and road change. Not judged: whether the pale realm props suit matrix and synthwave.
